title: Multiple Current Enhancement Regimes and Interaction Induced Re-entrant Transport in a Quasiperiodic Hubbard Ring with Antiferromagnetic Order
abstract: We investigate persistent charge and spin currents in a one-dimensional quantum ring threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm (AB) flux, considering generalized Aubry-André-Harper (AAH) modulation with staggered onsite energies and antiferromagnetic (AFM) ordering in both the noninteracting and interacting regimes, with the latter treated using a self-consistent Hartree-Fock mean field theory (MFT). At half filling, two distinct current-enhancement peaks emerge as the modulation strength increases, with quasiperiodic hopping modulation playing a crucial role in establishing the two-peak structure within a restricted parameter regime. Spin-resolved bond-current profiles reveal a switch in the dominant spin contribution between the two peaks, while the inverse participation ratio (IPR) and flux-dependent spin-resolved ground-state energies provide complementary insights into the spatial characteristics of the eigenstates and their spin-dependent flux sensitivity. At quarter filling, the spin current exhibits a single enhancement peak, in contrast to the two-peak response observed at half filling. The Hubbard interaction affects the two half-filled peaks differently: it suppresses the primary peak, whereas the secondary peak exhibits a nonmonotonic, re-entrant response, with the current recovering at finite interaction strength. The interacting results are further characterized through the Drude weight, and comparisons with exact diagonalization (ED) and density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations for a finite half-filled system support the reliability of the MFT description. Our findings elucidate how quasiperiodic modulation, AFM order, band filling, and electronic correlations collectively govern the magnitude and spin-resolved character of persistent currents, giving rise to multiple enhancement regimes and interaction-induced re-entrant behavior.
summary: This work explores persistent charge and spin currents in a quasiperiodic Hubbard ring with AFM order. The authors find that the system displays multiple current enhancement peaks, and critically, the Hubbard interaction causes a nonmonotonic, re-entrant current response in one of these peaks. The study highlights how quasiperiodicity, correlations, and magnetic order collectively dictate the transport properties.
main_problem: The study investigates persistent charge and spin currents in a quasiperiodic Hubbard ring subjected to antiferromagnetic ordering.
main_result: The system exhibits multiple current enhancement regimes dependent on modulation strength and filling, and the Hubbard interaction induces a nonmonotonic, re-entrant response in the secondary current peak at half-filling.
method: The analysis employs self-consistent Hartree-Fock mean-field theory (MFT) to treat the interacting Hubbard model, with results benchmarked against ED and DMRG.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional quantum ring threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm flux, featuring a generalized Aubry-André-Harper (AAH) modulation in both hopping and onsite energies, alongside an antiferromagnetic (AFM) staggered Zeeman field and Hubbard interaction.
key_observables: Persistent charge and spin currents ($I_c, I_s$), Drude weight, spin-resolved bond-current profiles, and Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR).
important_parameters: Quasiperiodic modulation strength ($W, V$), filling (half-filling vs. quarter-filling), and Hubbard interaction strength ($U$).
main_assumptions: The interacting regime is treated using the self-consistent Hartree-Fock mean-field approximation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the staggered AAH site-energy modulation and quasiperiodically modulated hopping in the system.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the model Hamiltonian, analyzes the non-interacting case, and then systematically investigates the effects of the Hubbard interaction ($U$) on the persistent currents, focusing on the differences between half-filling and quarter-filling.
why_interesting: The combination of quasiperiodicity, strong correlations (Hubbard model), and magnetic ordering provides a rich platform to study emergent transport phenomena like re-entrant behavior, which is highly relevant to correlated electron systems in engineered lattices.
